Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

some adjective and pronoun

a certain one or number, not named

also some … others, some people, some things, a few, some meat, some (amount of)

classical

Plin. Ep. 3.5.10: ut nōn aliquā parte prōdesset
Cic. Fin. 5.5: in aliquā historiā vestīgium pōnimus
Traupman 382

aliquī, aliqua, aliquod

adjective; plural aliquī, aliquae, aliqua; the pronoun is aliquis, aliquid · Declension on Wiktionary

some (or other)

A thing or person that exists, though it does not matter which (Lewis & Short s.v. aliquis; see someone, something). After sī, nisi, num, nē it loses its ali- (see any). English “some” before a mass noun (“some bread”) is usually left out in Latin, or said with paulum (see a little).

Other words

  • quīdam, quaedam, quoddam — some, a certain (known but not named)

    adjective and pronoun (neuter pronoun quiddam) · also used · classical · Mart. 1.16.1: sunt bona, sunt quaedam mediōcria

    In the plural, “some” set against others: sunt quaedam mediōcria, some are middling.

  • nōnnūllī, nōnnūllae, nōnnūlla — some, a fair number of

    adjective, mostly plural; also written apart, nōn nūllī · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.5.146: vīna nōn nūllī Graeca (Lewis & Short); Caes. BC 1.13.4: nōnnūlla pars mīlitum (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short (s.v. aliquot): nōnnūllī picks out an indefinite number from among several, “some of them”; aliquot is a small number (see several).

  • aliī … aliī — some … others

    plural of alius, repeated · also used · classical · Caes. BG 3.25: cum aliī fossās complērent, aliī dēfēnsōrēs vallō dēpellerent (Lewis & Short)

    “Some … others … others”: each group gets its own aliī; the last may be nōnnūllī or pars (Lewis & Short s.v. alius).

Examples

  • dīcere etiam solēbat nūllum esse librum tam malum ut nōn aliquā parte prōdesset

    he used to say, too, that no book was so bad as not to be useful in some partPlin. Ep. 3.5.10

  • aestātis mīra clēmentia: semper āēr spīritū aliquō movētur

    the summer is wonderfully mild: the air is always stirred by some breezePlin. Ep. 5.6.5

  • quācumque enim ingredimur, in aliquā historiā vestīgium pōnimus

    for wherever we walk, we set foot on some piece of historyCic. Fin. 5.5

  • sunt bona, sunt quaedam mediōcria, sunt mala plūra quae legis hīc

    some of what you read here is good, some middling, more of it badMart. 1.16.1–2

  • prōferēbant aliī purpuram, tūs aliī, gemmās aliī, vīna nōn nūllī Graeca

    some brought out purple cloth, others incense, others jewels, some Greek winesCic. Verr. 2.5.146 (Lewis & Short)

  • ex quō mihi inter virtūtēs grammaticī habēbitur aliqua nescīre

    so I shall count it among a teacher’s virtues not to know some thingsQuint. 1.8.21

  • aliquot

    some (a number of)Traupman 382

  • aliquid carnis

    some meatTraupman 382

See also someone, something, any, a little, several.
